source.title: Risk and Refusal: Mechanisms of LLM Responses to Suicidal Ideation
source.authors: Drishti Goel; Soorya Ram Shimgekar; Jeongah Lee; Violeta J. Rodríguez; Daniel S. Brown; Ravi Karkar; Koustuv Saha

record.tranche_reason: The study constructs a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction following the original method and causally intervenes on it, including ablation after every layer at all token positions. It tests refusal on generic instructions and SI disclosures, and tests direction addition on generic harmless instructions.
record.gate_note: Rows focus on the direction interventions and their refusal and response-risk outcomes. The paper also reports behavioral effects of classification and clinician guidance, but those do not themselves intervene on the refusal direction. The exploratory attribution graphs concern other models and are described as non-causal; they are not rows for the refusal-direction claim.
record.test_reason: The study rebuilds the Arditi et al. difference-in-means direction (self-harm items removed) in Phi-4-mini and Llama-3.1-8B. It ablates it at every layer and adds it at one layer, with matched-norm random controls, and scores refusal on held-out generic instructions (Table 11). It then applies the same interventions to SI disclosures (Tables 1, 12, 13), a new setting with results on V1. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a generic refusal direction predicts and causally contributes to SI refusals, but ablating it raises engagement without reliably lowering response risk. Clinician guidance lowers both refusal and risk, acting partly along the refusal direction (reciprocal ±g effects in Phi-4-mini, not direction-specific in Llama) and partly through other changes.
record.recipe_differences: The direction is the harmful-minus-harmless mean activation difference following Arditi et al. (2024), with suicide/self-harm examples excluded and five high-mean-absolute-activation coordinates masked at each layer. The main ablation is applied after the embedding and every transformer layer at all token positions; causal tests focus on two models.
record.method_sensitivity: The causal intervention is performed at layer 16 for Phi-4-mini and layer 18 for Llama-3.1-8B. A Phi-4-mini robustness check using a generic-validation-selected layer-21 direction is reported in Table 13; the paper says causal effects largely replicate, while the Baseline −g result is only partly direction-specific. Effects also vary by model and SI dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the refusal direction on SI disclosures raised RubRIX-flagged responses in 5 of 6 model–dataset cells (e.g., 44.7→71.4%). Mean flagged items rose significantly. Explicit naming of suicide risk also fell.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing the refusal direction raises engagement but does not make responses to sensitive disclosures safer; response risk rises.

fits_no_version.finding: A direction built without SI data predicts baseline refusal of SI disclosures (AUROC 0.68–0.94) and its ablation removes those refusals (Table 3, Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generic harmful-request refusal direction also mediates refusal of non-request distress disclosures (over-refusal transfer across content types).

fits_no_version.finding: Clinician guidance lowers refusal-direction projections. Subtracting or adding back the guidance shift g changes refusal reciprocally in Phi-4-mini but not direction-specifically in Llama-3.1-8B (Tables 1, 14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-based guidance reduces refusal partly by moving activations along the refusal direction, with model-dependent specificity.

record.problems: Causal interventions focus on two open-weight models chosen for appreciable baseline refusal. SI interventions use refusal-enriched subsets, not an unselected sample. Response risk and refusal are assessed by GPT-5-nano judges; the authors note these measures do not establish real-world support outcomes. General capability preservation is not broadly tested; the reported degeneration measure is limited. Intervention analyses are uncorrected, and some risk-prevalence comparisons have no stated significance test.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the reported generic held-out refusal and SI ablation results. The paper also reports a multi-strength direction-addition sweep under clinician guidance (Table 12), layer-21 robustness results (Table 13), and ±g guidance-shift interventions (Tables 1 and 14); these were left out to prioritize the direct removal/addition tests on refusal and the principal SI risk outcomes.

untested.parts: Preservation of broad capabilities: no capability benchmark; only a degeneracy heuristic is reported. Only two models are tested causally.

missing.what: Phi-4-mini any-refusal after refusal-direction ablation on SI disclosures: 35.3→18.6, 37.4→14.1, 39.9→10.1 (random 31.4, 35.9, 36.2)
Degeneration under ablation on harmful instructions (Phi 6→3%, Llama 1→0%), i.e. no degradation from ablation

Direction-addition sweep on SI posts under guidance (+0.25/+0.5/+0.75). Phi refusal rose to 70–94%, with degeneration up to 75.5% at +0.75. Llama refusal stayed low until +0.75 (23–70%). Random addition gave no rise.
Layer-21 robustness check: Phi ablation drops any refusal 35.3→9.3 and explicit 19.7→0.0; random ablation 32.7

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T1 covers the generic-instruction replication; the SI-disclosure results are effectively a T3 extension. RubRIX rows are relinked to none because response-risk on disclosures is not refusal or general capability. Three random-control rows had wrong significance values. Intervention tests are uncorrected, and the judges are GPT-5-nano.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test preservation of broad general capabilities with a broad capability benchmark; response risk and degeneration are limited outcome measures. Direction addition is tested on generic harmless instructions, not as a systematic survey of harmless tasks.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is evaluated.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is evaluated.
The study does not compare a single direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple-direction model of refusal.
The study measures recognition of SI/self-harm risk and refusal behavior, but does not independently intervene on or measure harmfulness judgment as distinct from the refusal decision.
No language transfer, base-to-instruct transfer, or systematic model-variant transfer is tested.
No refusal-training method, timing, or training stage is varied.

relation.reason: Its own ablation and addition results (Tables 1, 11, 12, 13) bear directly on whether the direction mediates refusal.

tranche.reason: Table 11 rebuilds the Arditi et al. difference-in-means direction from Arditi's splits. It ablates at all layers and positions, adds at one layer, and scores held-out harmful/harmless instructions by Arditi's substring criterion (same method and measure), with matched-norm random controls. It then extends this to SI disclosures.

source_check.notes: The checked rows do not include Table 12 (addition on guided SI disclosures, n=200, +0.25/+0.5/+0.75). There Phi degeneration reaches 36.5–42% at +0.5 and 62.5–75.5% at +0.75 on SH-Det/X-Sens, while Llama induces 23–70% at +0.75 with ≤0.5% degeneration. Also not covered: Table 13 (Phi layer-21 replication) and Table 14 (±g random controls). The "+0.5 r" scale is not defined against a natural norm. There are no capability benchmarks; ablation raised RubRIX risk (e.g. Phi Reddit mean flagged items 0.74→1.28***).
